The #NHLJets had 87 shot attempts tonight -- 47 on goal, 24 blocked, 16 missed.  Kyle Connor led the way with 15 attempts, while Cole Perfetti (12) and Mark Scheifele (11) were in double digits as well.   Nino Niederreiter 0 attempts in 6:25 of ice time. Haydn Fleury 0 in 7:36.

#NHLJets coach Scott Arniel on Montreal rookie goaltender Jacob Fowler, who held Winnipeg at bay for more than 57 minutes before the dam burst:  "That young Fowler kid. Wow, that's twice now I've seen him. I don't want to see him anymore. Wow, he's something."

A Montreal scribe to #NHLJets Scott Arniel.   "You came in with questions about your future..."  Arniel interjects.   “No, no, no. You came in with questions about my future. I really don’t care about that. I really don’t. I’m so happy that we won tonight. We got that win."

#NHLJets GM Kevin Cheveldayoff to me in the elevator as we headed down to the room.  "I love when you have to re-write your story."  The fact Winnipeg and Montreal are now in the same time zone did me no favours with pressing print deadline and a stunning turn of events.

What a visual here in Montreal as Tyrel Bauer, blood literally dripping from that hands, speaks about the #NHLJets historic comeback win and his Gordie Howe hatty that helped spark it.  “I don’t think I’ve ever wanted to win a game more.”
#NHLJets Kyle Connor said this is the type of win he hopes “can catapult” his team going forward. He points to Tyrel Bauer - “the ultimate teammate - for lighting the fuse.
